info.name: Umrah Scanner API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Umrah Scanner marketplace backend (Spring Boot 4 / Java 17, Clean Architecture, feature-based modules).

## Running this collection end to end
1. Boot the app with the `dev` profile active so `/auth/dev-google-test` exists (`SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=dev ./gradlew bootRun`) — it never exists otherwise.
2. Run **Auth > Dev Login - Customer** and **Auth > Dev Login - Company** — these auto-capture tokens into collection variables via their Tests scripts.
3. Run **Company > Register Company**, then bootstrap an admin token per the instructions on the two **Dev Login - Admin** requests, then **Admin: Approve Company**.
4. Run **Trip > Create Trip**, **Upsert Room Prices** (see Known Issues — the write succeeds even though this call currently 500s), **Publish Trip** — all auto-capture `tripId`.
5. Run **Company > Admin: Set Company Commission Per Traveler** — leads created before a rate is set price at zero commission and zero cashback, permanently.
6. Run **Lead > Contact Company** (as customer, with traveler counts) to create a lead, then run the numbered requests 1–7 in that folder in order — they walk the same lead from INTERESTED through PENDING_DEPOSIT_CONFIRMATION, DEPOSIT_PAID, PENDING_FULL_PAYMENT_CONFIRMATION, FULLY_PAID, PENDING_COMMISSION_CONFIRMATION, COMMISSION_PAID and CASHBACK_PAID. A review can be submitted any time from DEPOSIT_PAID onwards — it no longer has to wait for the payout chain to finish.

Every request that needs a specific role's token references a collection variable (`{{customerAccessToken}}`, `{{companyAccessToken}}`, `{{adminAccessToken}}`) as its own Authorization — set once by the login requests' Tests scripts, used everywhere else.

## Two requests are deliberately terminal
**Admin: Suspend Company** and **Delete Trip (soft delete)** are placed last in their folders on purpose — running either one breaks every later request in this collection that depends on that company/trip still being usable (there is no un-suspend or undelete endpoint). Skip them while you're still exploring; run them last, or against a disposable trip/company, when you specifically want to see that behavior.

## Known live issues found while validating this collection
Running every request against the real API (via Newman) surfaced two confirmed, reproducible bugs in the backend itself — not in these requests:

1. **Update Trip silently deletes all of a trip's hotels when `hotels` is omitted (`null`).** `TripController.toHotelInputs()` converts a null `hotels` list into an *empty* list before it reaches the use case, so `UpdateTripUseCase`'s `if (command.hotels() != null)` guard sees a non-null empty list, clears the existing hotels, and adds none back. Verified by direct DB inspection: hotel count went from 2 to 0 after an Update Trip call that sent `hotels: null` expecting them to be left alone.
2. **Update Trip and Upsert Room Prices both throw a 500 even when the underlying write succeeds.** Both use cases fetch the trip via a plain lazy query with no entity graph; the controller then builds `TripDetailResponse`, which touches *both* `hotels` and `roomPrices` — but each use case only happens to initialize whichever one it itself mutated, so accessing the other throws `LazyInitializationException: no session`. Confirmed by DB inspection that Upsert Room Prices' write actually commits (room_prices rows exist) despite the client receiving a 500.
3. Sending a *populated* `hotels` list to Update Trip hits a third, different error: a `uq_trip_hotels_trip_city` duplicate-key violation, because Hibernate inserts the replacement rows before deleting the orphaned old ones for the same (trip_id, city).

Net effect: **Update Trip cannot currently be called successfully at all** if the trip has hotels — every path (send hotels, omit hotels) fails, and omitting them actively destroys data rather than leaving it untouched. This needs a real code fix, not a workaround in this collection.

A third, independent instance of the same root cause: **Add Favourite** always returns 500 (confirmed) — the trip/customer are attached via `getReferenceById` with no eager fetch, then the response mapper reads trip fields after the transaction has closed. **List Favourites** works because its query already carries an `@EntityGraph` on `trip`; the write path never got the same treatment.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Google login (production), the dev-only bypass, refresh, and logout.

request.description: Bypasses real Google verification — only exists when the app is booted with `--spring.profiles.active=dev` AND `app.dev-auth.enabled=true` (the dev profile sets this automatically via application-dev.properties). In any other profile this path returns 401 (no controller is even registered). Creates the customer account on first call; later calls with the same email log back into the same account.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Same dev-only bypass, creating/logging into the COMPANY-role account used through the rest of this collection.

response.name: 200 OK

item.name: Dev Login - Admin, Step 1: create the account

request.description:
There is no API that creates an ADMIN account — by design, only COMPANY/CUSTOMER can self-register (see LoginWithGoogleUseCase). To get an admin token for local testing:

1. Run this request once (creates a normal CUSTOMER-role row for {{adminEmail}}).
2. Promote it directly in your local dev Postgres:
   `UPDATE users SET role = 'ADMIN' WHERE email = '{{adminEmail}}';`
3. Run **Dev Login - Admin, Step 2** below to mint a token reflecting the new role.

response.name: 200 OK

item.name: Dev Login - Admin, Step 2: after promoting in DB

request.description: Run only after the SQL UPDATE described in Step 1 — the existing user is found by email, so `role` here is ignored; the token now carries ADMIN.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: The real login path — needs a genuine Google ID token from the mobile app's Google Sign-In SDK, so it can't be exercised as-is from Postman. `role` only matters the first time a given Google account logs in (COMPANY or CUSTOMER; ADMIN is rejected).

item.name: Lead
item.description: The booking lifecycle: INTERESTED → PENDING_DEPOSIT_CONFIRMATION → DEPOSIT_PAID → PENDING_FULL_PAYMENT_CONFIRMATION → FULLY_PAID → PENDING_COMMISSION_CONFIRMATION → COMMISSION_PAID → CASHBACK_PAID. Whoever reports a payment first decides the path: a customer report parks the lead in the matching PENDING_* state until the other side confirms, while a company (or, for commission, an admin) recording it goes straight to the settled state. Set the company's commission (Company folder) before creating a lead, or it will price at zero. Traveler counts stay editable until FULLY_PAID — always read the lead's travelersEditable flag.

request.description: Creates the lead and permanently fixes its commission and cashback for these traveler counts. adultCount is the billable traveler count — commission = the company's commissionPerTraveler x adultCount, and cashback is a quarter of that. Idempotent: contacting the same trip again returns the existing lead (refreshing the counts only while it is still before FULLY_PAID). Company identity becomes visible on this trip for this customer from here on.
